analysis:
The PR changes only docs/threat-model.yaml: a header comment (lines 46-49) and a rewrite of TB-012 (lines 816-867). It updates T-059 and adds T-060 in a part of the file past the supplied excerpt (changed head ranges 2349-2398), so those threat entries were not visible to me. TB-012 documents the new operator mailbox and accept-time peer verification, which runs before a connection takes one of eight slots. It also records the DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET override, self-reported busy fields, the fail-open hold record, request timeouts (10s/8KiB, 300s idle) and O_NOFOLLOW-style file reads.

The edit is documentation only. It adds no code and changes no controls, so there is no security regression in the supplied evidence. The docs state several residual risks plainly, which is appropriate: same-UID tampering; no bound on a held machine lock; the fail-open hold record; accept-thread flooding; and unverifiable busy fields.

Open points for the next pass, none of which is a finding:
- The DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET override is honored in every build (line 835). The doc says the LaunchAgent does not pass it. Whether a same-UID process can influence the provider's environment is not shown in the supplied evidence.
- The mailbox 'process identity' binding and 60s validity could not be verified against the Swift source (ProviderCore/Service/LifecycleMailbox.swift), which was not supplied.
- The T-059 and T-060 text and the A-018 notes were not visible in the excerpt.
- The doc claims a hold never sends provider_drain or stops the App Attest worker. That is a code claim I cannot confirm here.
- The doc says the coordinator cannot verify why a provider stopped taking work (A-018). Handling of the busy fields is platform-owned and out of scope here.

No canonical threat-model invariants (TB-002, TB-003, TB-009) are weakened by the visible text.
